caption: Is R68 000 a lot, or does it just disappear faster than it looks? What's your honest answer?

slides.title:
How we spend our
R68 000 household
income
Living in Somerset West
slides.body:
Him 45, her 43
Married, three kids (16, 13 and 8)
Jobs: Pharmacy manager & part-time physiotherapist
Combined net: R68 000 p/m

slides.title: Bond repayment
slides.body: We bought in 2019. The house is worth more than we paid. It doesn't feel like it when the bond leaves.

slides.title: School fees
slides.includes: Two kids at a private school, one at a public school
slides.body: The private fees are R6 300 each. The public school is R1 600 a month. The gap is real.

slides.title: Medical aid
slides.body: We'd drop to a cheaper plan if his scripts weren't what they are.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Family of five, a teenager who eats a lot
slides.body: We shop twice a week. The teen shops with us. This is the rule.

slides.title: Car instalments & petrol
slides.includes: His SUV, her hatchback, school run twice a day
slides.body: We've talked about selling one car a few times. We keep not doing it.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: domestic help, black tax, electricity and water, funeral policies, fibre and DStv, extra-murals, eating out
slides.body: Seven lines, R9 400. The eating out is R3 800 and I'd rather not defend it.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R68 000. On paper a high income. In practice one bad month wipes the buffer.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
We uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and compared our budget with what we actually spent.

The gap was the school run and the eating out.

No bank login needed.
